before_times: for you, your child, or someone you help (a care home resident)
which visit: an eye exam, a contact lens fitting too, or an eye problem visit (the office's own visit types; never a symptom typed into the AI)
a vision plan or medical insurance (its name only), or paying yourself
after_time: anything the office should know to help, like a wheelchair or needing an interpreter
for a care home or school visit: the place's name, the room, and who meets the eye doctor
secure_page_only: plan member ID, the plan holder and a photo of the card (the vision plan, or the medical insurance for an eye problem)
health history: medicines, allergies, eye conditions, diabetes
current glasses and contact lens details (the brand and power from the box), and the last eye exam date
a parent's or guardian's consent for anyone under 18, or the consent of the person who decides for an adult who can't
intake_questions.never_asked: Rosie never asks for symptoms, reasons, results or prescriptions in the AI chat; what a patient types anyway is checked for danger, and the details go only to the secure page
intake_questions.who_may_book: an adult for themselves; a parent or guardian for anyone under 18; a guardian or health care agent for an adult who can't consent; the care home's staff for a resident, with the decider's consent on the secure page; a minor alone only where the state's rules let minors consent to eye care (a switch)

stop.words: sudden vision loss, sudden flashes of light, or a shadow or curtain across the vision
stop.say: This needs care now. Go to the nearest emergency room or call 911. Don't wait for an eye visit.
stop.booking: no booking; the same words are repeated if a same-day request is declined, and if it starts before a booked visit (the visit stays booked and the owner is told)

stop.words: a chemical splash in the eye, or something stuck in it
stop.say: Rinse a chemical splash with clean running water right away, and call Poison Help at 1-800-222-1222 or 911. Don't rub something stuck in the eye: go to the emergency room or call 911.
stop.booking: no booking; the words are fixed and the same for everyone

stop.words: an eye hit hard or cut, or sudden bad eye pain with a headache or throwing up
stop.say: This needs care now. Go to the nearest emergency room or call 911.

go_on.words: red, itchy, sore or dry eyes with nothing else
go_on.what: matched to the office's own eye problem visit; Rosie never judges how urgent it is, and same-day times need the owner's OK

safety_and_stop_words.always: the general screen: danger to life, fire, gas or a medical emergency gets 911, and words about self-harm get 988

steps.name: Health history, consent and the plan's papers
steps.when: on the secure page only, never by text; due the day before the visit (a same-day visit: before the time is held); one reminder before it's due
steps.who: every new patient; returning patients once a year, or when their health changes
steps.result: not done by its due date: Sam keeps the visit (signed on the secure page at the desk or the door, before any pre-test), moves it, or cancels with no fee

steps.name: The plan check
steps.when: while booking, by the front desk, by hand
steps.who: every patient who names a plan
steps.result: covered; some services only (like a contact lens fitting the plan won't pay); not covered; or can't check now (the desk checks later, and the patient may cancel free); the plan's exam not due yet: keep the time at the office's own price, or move it to the date the plan allows

steps.name: A written price estimate for self-pay patients
steps.when: told while booking; sent within 1 business day (the example office's rule), or sooner where the rules require it
steps.result: a to-do for the front desk, with its due date

steps.name: The care home's or school's OK
steps.who: the host place agrees to host the visits
steps.result: no OK: no times at that place

first_steps_and_forms.prep: bring your glasses, your contact lens box or its prescription, a photo ID and the plan card; the eyes may be dilated and stay blurry and light-sensitive for a few hours, so bring sunglasses and plan a ride home; at a care home: the medicine list ready with the nurse

staff.skills: eye doctors: exams, contact lens fittings, dilating drops, eye problem visits and prescriptions; opticians: pre-tests, frames and lenses, glasses fittings and repairs, and teaching contact lens care; only people cleared for visits away go to care homes and schools
staff.licenses_or_certificates: each optometrist's own license, per state; opticians only where the state licenses them
staff.supervision: an optician's pre-tests are read by the eye doctor; which tests an optician may run comes from the state form (a switch)
staff.who_oks: the owner OKs same-day eye problem visits, and anything an optician flags
staff.stand_in: an eye doctor out: another eye doctor takes the exam, or new times; an optician out: the eye doctor runs the pre-tests, and the glasses desk waits; a one-doctor day means new times for that day's patients

children_and_age.who_may_book: an adult for themselves; a parent or guardian for anyone under 18; a guardian or health care agent for an adult who can't consent; the care home's staff for a resident, with the decider's consent on the secure page; a minor alone only where the state's rules let minors consent to eye care (a switch)
children_and_age.minors_texts: a minor's texts go to the parent or guardian; a minor who may consent alone gets texts only on their own phone, with no visit type
children_and_age.minors_rules: who may consent for a minor, and at what age a minor may consent alone (a switch from the state form)

visit.check_in: at the office: the check-in code at the front desk; at a care home or school: the code from the patient, or from the nurse or staff member named on the booking
visit.done: the check-in code or DONE; the eye doctor's notes, results and prescriptions stay in the office's own records, never in Rosie or a text
visit.changes_at_visit: an extra test, like a retina photo, is priced and OK'd before it's done; a medical problem found at a routine exam may move the visit to the medical plan, with the share shown first
visit.before_work: the optician reads the health history and asks about changes before any test

license.note: Optional. Upload anything. Rosie never checks it and never shows it as checked (D96).
license.need: always: each optometrist holds their own active license from the state's optometry board
license.who: each person; opticians only where the state licenses them (a switch from the state form); the practice too where the state's form registers eye care offices or their owners
license.ask: each optometrist's license number in their invite reply (or the owner sends it); an optician's license number where the state asks; the practice's registration from the owner
license.insurance: malpractice insurance where the state's form asks for it

never_in_a_text: texts carry only the practice's name, the date, the time, the address and a secure link: never the visit type, the plan, the reason, results or a prescription; at the office, not the eye doctor's name either; when the eye doctor or optician comes to a care home, school or home, their name stays, for the door check; a READY text says only that the order is ready to pick up
